candidates.change_summary: Change owner() to return tx.origin instead of the stored _owner, causing a different returned address in many call contexts.
Removed the require that newOwner is non-zero, allowing transferOwnership to set owner to zero address (renounce via transfer).
Add an extra check that newOwner must be equal to the current owner, preventing any change unless newOwner matches current owner (effectively forbids changing owner to anyone else).
Tighten onlyOwner to require msg.sender equals owner and also that owner is not the zero address, which will block calls when owner is zero.
Change paused() to return the inverse of the internal _paused flag so callers observe the opposite paused state.

Change setKeeper to only allow the owner to set keeper by adding onlyOwner modifier to the function declaration (prevents non-owner from changing keeper), altering observable behavior of keeper after call.
Prevent nullifying keeper by disallowing zero address; require new keeper is non-zero before assignment (calls with zero no longer change keeper).
Relax onlyOwner check to compare against tx.origin instead of _msgSender(), allowing transactions forwarded by contracts to bypass owner restriction and change keeper.
Replace the assignment to slippageThresholdGmxBps with assignment to slippageThresholdGmxBps + 1, so the stored threshold differs from the input.
Replace the assignment to slippageThresholdGmxBps with assignment to half the provided value, changing stored threshold.
Replace the assignment to slippageThresholdGmxBps with assignment to a fixed constant 0, so the stored threshold becomes zero regardless of input.
Replace the assignment to slippageThresholdGmxBps with assignment to the maximum BPS constant, making stored threshold always MAX_BPS.

Change the owner check to compare against tx.origin instead of msg.sender, allowing different callers to pass the onlyOwner guard and thus enabling non-owner to call setThresholds which changes slippageThresholdGmxBps via public surface.
